Decentralization of manufacturing from base cities to suburbs is demonstrated by Table 3. 5/ Shown is the percentage increase in manufacturing employment from 1958-1967 in central cities and suburbs at 37 metropolitan areas. This vividly illustrates the suburban gains achieved relative to usually low gains (or losses) in manufacturing employment in cities.

The outward migration from city to suburbs of commercial, industrial and institutional activities is further exhibited in Table 4. 6 / This shows percentages of private nonresidential construction in the suburbs during 1954-1965 and 1960-1965 periods by type of construction. From 1960-1965, more than 50 percent of the investment in industrial construction was in the suburbs for each of the thirteen cities listed in the table.
